newsitem.title: USA: Convicted rapist cannot be forced to apologize.
newsitem.headline: Convicted rapist cannot be forced to apologize.

text.p: A judge was wrong in ordering a New Mexico man to apologise as part of his sentence for raping a woman, a federal appeals court ruled Monday.
"To extract an apology ... would seem to impinge on his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination," the 10th Circuit Court of Appeals said.
U.S. District Judge James Parker in Albuquerque had required the man, Christopher Acevedo, to apologise in addition to serving almost 20 years in prison followed by five years of supervised release.
The apology was to be made at the end of the prison term.
Acevedo claimed at his trial that the sex was consensual, but the victim testified he forced the sex by threatening her with a knife.

Although the apology would not have been voluntary, it might be used to charge him with perjury for testifying the sex was consensual, the court said. It also said the victim might improperly use the apology in a civil lawsuit.
The case was in federal court because the crime occured on Indian tribal land which is subject to federal jurisdiction.
